newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 20.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Four thousand graduates and 8,000 GCE O/L and A/L qualified youth to enter private sector in '97, after comprehensive vocational training, says President Kumaratunga. The first batch of 38 grduates who completed training, were given letters of appointment in the private sector, on Thursday.
The special presidential commission inquiring into the death of senior politician Lalith Athulathmudali, summons United National Party (UNP) stalwart Sirisena Cooray to appear, on January 9, 1997.
Shell Gas Lanka contemplating gas price hike in January, say sources.
Lalith Athulathmudali commission summons former UNP cabinet minister, Sirisena Cooray to appear on January 9.
A Sri Lanka Air Force Mi24 helicopter attacks and kills about 30 LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam) rebels in operations in the east, say defence sources.
About 40 trade unions to protest at noon opposite Colombo's Fort railway station, against privatisation.
Recent military operations against the LTTE in the east, seriously disrupts rebel communications, throwing them into disarray, say defence sources.
Sixteen Sinhalese fishermen who were held captive by Tamil rebels, released on Thursday to the International Red Cross.
Malaria spreads in northern Wanni area, affecting nerly 10 percent of the refugees, say doctors in the area.
Forces destroy 175 coffins in eastern Paduvankarai rebel camp, recently captured by them in an operation.
